convention: Each formula is a JS expression evaluated with vm.runInNewContext(formula, {...params}); bare param names; result must deep-equal value.

sources.BPP99: Bagust A, Place M, Posnett JW. Dynamics of bed use in accommodating emergency admissions: stochastic simulation model. BMJ 1999;319(7203):155-158. doi:10.1136/bmj.319.7203.155 (abstract: risks discernible above about 85 % average occupancy; regular bed shortages and periodic bed crises at 90 % or more)
sources.KH03: NHS England, Bed Availability and Occupancy (KH03), Quarter 3 2023-24 Statistical Press Notice (Feb 2024): general and acute beds open overnight, average occupancy 92.0 % in Quarter 3 2022/23 (Oct-Dec 2022, revised data)
sources.KL75: Kleinrock L. Queueing Systems, Volume 1: Theory. Wiley, 1975. M/M/1: mean wait in queue Wq = rho/(1-rho) x mean service time; by PASTA an arrival finds on average rho/(1-rho) jobs in the system
sources.KI61: Kingman JFC. The single server queue in heavy traffic. Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 1961;57:902-904 (wait grows as rho/(1-rho), scaled by arrival and service variability)
sources.RE09: Reinertsen DG. The Principles of Product Development Flow: Second Generation Lean Product Development. Celeritas, 2009. Ch. 3 'Managing Queues' (from p. 53): queue size against capacity utilization
sources.SIM: Seeded simulation in this claim's formula: M/M/1, mulberry32(seed), exponential gaps and job sizes from one stream (common random numbers for both desks), arrivals scaled by 1/rho, mean job size 1, warm-up jobs discarded, then n jobs counted; 'jobs ahead' = jobs in the system (waiting or in service) at the instant of arrival. Seed rule: the first seed from 1 upward whose two counts both land within 10 % of the long-run n x rho/(1-rho)
